indicators.note: in tells us the word for minute sits inside the word for a relative

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
a mo is a moment, a minute, as in 'just a mo'

explanation.surface: A physicist talks about a tiny quantity within relativistic mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective meaning tiny, but it is the noun, a short moment: MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of something is a quantity or quantity of material, the same idea as a total or sum.

indicators.note: mixing tells us to stir the letters of the preceding words into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone vows not to mix their drinks tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' rearranges the letters of I SHAN'T BE; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong anise-flavoured spirit, an example of a drink.

parts.note: something plain to see is overt, open and obvious
an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: A shopper returns a plain vase to the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like a description of the vase but is a synonym for OVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a ruling or decision is to reverse it, as an appeal court reverses a verdict.

explanation.surface: A warning that fraud ends in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: to nick is to steal, and 'the nick' is prison or a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for stealing something, and British slang for a jail or police cells.

clue.text: Many of our men used by American

indicators.note: used here means worked over or reshaped, so the letters of our men are rearranged

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Lots of British soldiers are deployed by the Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' reads as 'employed' in the surface, but here it means worked over, so it is the signal to rearrange OUR MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous is a plain synonym for great in number, plentiful.

clue.text: Out of control Iran sent rude broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the three words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report of a rude message sent by Iran, out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a news word but rearranges the letters of IRAN SENT RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained behaviour is unchecked, with no restraint holding it back.

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the fruit is removed

parts.note: a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: A remark that all fruit has had its top cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every both refer to all members of a group taken one by one.

indicators.note: After tells us the remaining pieces come once the word for work is placed

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral for one
ingested means ate

explanation.surface: After work, someone swallowed some drug.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium, such as morphine.

parts.note: to look at something is to see it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone reads an article and gets angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To fume and to seethe both mean to be inwardly furious.

clue.text: Drawing ship on top of sea

indicators.note: on tells us the ship comes on, that is after, the letter from sea
top of picks the first letter of the word sea

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing ship

explanation.surface: An artist's picture of a ship riding on the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat; it follows S, the first letter of 'sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or preliminary picture.

indicators.note: catching means the word for worth holds the word for show inside it

parts.note: the price of something is its worth
an act is a show or performance

explanation.surface: A theatre rehearsal is worth seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice is a run-through to improve, which is what a rehearsal is.

clue.text: Labour with scanty reform for police

indicators.note: reform means the letters are formed anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: The Labour Party proposes reform of a thinly staffed police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' looks political but rearranges the letters of LABOUR and SCANTY ('with' is a link).
explanation.definitionFit: A constabulary is a police force, especially a British county force.

clue.text: Brown turning on old military alliance

indicators.note: turning means the word for brown is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown changes his view on an old defence pact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' suggests the politician but is the colour TAN, turned to NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is a defence pact between Western nations.

clue.text: Support Tory leader after disapproving noises

indicators.note: after places the leader of Tory behind the word for jeers

parts.note: boos are noises of disapproval

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: Backing for the Conservative leader after he has been jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost something is to give it a lift, to support or encourage it.

clue.text: State of Uruguay with Panama's backing?

parts.note: U is the international vehicle code for Uruguay

indicators.note: backing means the word for a Panama is reversed

parts.note: a Panama is a hat

explanation.surface: Asks whether Uruguay has the support of Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country but is a straw hat; HAT reversed gives TAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA.

indicators.note: Turn over means the word for bar is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise

explanation.surface: A pub turns its bar over to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but is a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively celebration, a festive gathering.

parts.note: a leg is a member, a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament is a Liberal sitting on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP but is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legal is lawful, within one's rights, so permitted or proper.

clue.text: Here, let's try a new treatment

definitions.text: Here, let's try a new treatment

indicators.note: new treatment means the preceding letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient is offered a new treatment at a doctor's.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: HARLEY STREET is the London street famous for private doctors, where a new treatment might be tried.
explanation.definitionFit: A London street lined with private medical practices, a place to go for treatment.

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for safe goes round the word in

parts.note: secure means safe

explanation.surface: A secure position at an easy job.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post that pays but demands little work.

clue.text: Unseemly move to right gripping church

indicators.note: gripping means the word for moving text right holds the church letters inside

parts.note: to indent text is to move it in from the left margin
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An indecent attempt to move to the right while holding on to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent conduct is improper and offends propriety.

indicators.note: Strange signals that the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An odd sheen on an iced cake's topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' suggests cake icing but is British slang for killing, here beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for executing them; beheading is one way of doing it.

clue.text: Whined and worried about party leader

indicators.note: about means the word for worried goes around the leading letter

parts.note: to have cared is to have worried

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word party

explanation.surface: Someone complained and fretted about the party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping is nagging complaint, so having carped is having grumbled.

indicators.note: In tells us the answer is concealed inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A minister issues a paper in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across parliamenT HE'S ISsuing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a dissertation or academic paper.

clue.text: Initially aspirin can help extreme pain

indicators.note: Initially tells us to take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Aspirin can help with severe pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

parts.note: a cur is a worthless person
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A worthless reporter is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' suggests drunk but means preserved, as meat is cured.
explanation.definitionFit: Curing food means preserving it by salting, smoking or pickling.

indicators.note: For the audience means the word for top is heard rather than read

parts.note: a peak is a top or summit

explanation.surface: A show's best dog performs for the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peke is a Pekingese, a small breed of dog.

parts.note: too means excessively, extremely

explanation.surface: A very big helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter but means an axe; 'perhaps' shows it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe or chopper is an example of a tool for cutting.

explanation.surface: Someone feels sad and unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off colour' suggests unwell but means risqué, as a blue joke is.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down or low in spirits; and smutty or racy, as in blue jokes.

parts.note: prior means earlier, past
oral means spoken aloud

explanation.surface: A monastery's prior gives his sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' suggests a monk but means earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral refers to a minister's care of their flock, so it is priestly.

indicators.note: said means the word for scratches is spoken out loud

parts.note: to claw is to scratch

explanation.surface: Someone scrawls notes on a paragraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a section of a legal document, like a numbered paragraph.

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
to splay is to spread out

explanation.surface: Police officers fan out among the protest marches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demos' suggests protest marches but means demonstrations, as in shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a demonstration, a showing of how something works.

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A student hates a French exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe, to dislike intensely.
